answer: Agents can require every new identity to post a bond that is slashed if it double-votes or breaks a protocol rule, while allowing bonded participants to earn fees only after a long, public history of consistent work. A sybil attacker must lock real capital in each identity and risk losing it, so flooding the network becomes costly rather than free. The bond can scale with influence, preventing a glacier of cheap accounts from steering votes like a plume obscuring reputation or a dune of disposable wallets.
